questions.q: How do one-star reviews affect restaurant sales?
questions.a: One-star reviews lower your rating, push you down in local search and shape a guest's first impression before they visit. That means fewer people find you and fewer choose you at the moment of decision. Across many locations, the lost traffic adds up to a real revenue leak.

questions.q: What causes most one-star restaurant reviews?
questions.a: Most come from preventable experiences, such as long waits, slow service, staff unprepared to handle concerns, wrong orders or unclean spaces. Feeling ignored or dismissed is another common trigger. Because these are operational patterns, you can find and fix them by looking for themes across reviews.

questions.q: How should I respond to a one-star review?
questions.a: Reply quickly with a personal, specific message that acknowledges the problem and shows what you'll do about it. Give local managers brand-approved language so the reply sounds human and consistent. For serious cases, follow up privately as well, since making it right offline often wins the guest back.

questions.q: How do I stop getting so many one-star reviews?
questions.a: Start by auditing your ratings and response times across every channel and location. Then look for patterns in the complaints, such as speed, service, quality or cleanliness, because those themes usually point to fixable operational issues. Fixing the root cause at each location reduces new one-star reviews, while fast replies help recover the guests who already left one.

questions.q: How can AI help manage negative reviews across locations?
questions.a: AI can scan reviews from Google, Yelp, Facebook and other sites in real time, flag urgent ones by tone and rating, and suggest replies your team can send quickly. It can also route operational issues to the right team so they're fixed at the source. Momos customers use this kind of workflow to respond faster and recover more unhappy guests.
